headline: The reviews already know Samuel. Sunday still looks like a walk-in.
summary: This is a real mother-and-son shop for nervous dogs, kennel-free, with a 5.0 Yelp page. The phone is the door. Directories print Sunday 8 to 6 like a walk-in salon. The site never prints a week. A neighbor with an anxious dog can drive to Arnold Way on a day the chair is not staffed for drop-ins.

signals.note: You show up for dog grooming in Alpine. Yelp is 5.0 from about 14 reviews, and people already ask for Samuel by name. A neighbor looking for a quiet groomer can find you.
signals.next: Keep the category pet groomer in Alpine. Kennel-free and special-needs should stay in the listing, not just the about page.

signals.note: The number (619) 509-8333 is consistent. The contact page uses info@csgalpine.com. Call or text is how people actually book. That door works.
signals.next: Keep that number on every listing. Do not add a second one.

signals.note: Yahoo and MapQuest print Tuesday through Sunday 8 to 6, Monday closed. Yelp has shown closed until 8 and open until 6. The site does not print a week. The FAQ says appointments preferred, walk-ins call ahead. A map that looks like Sunday walk-in is how a nervous dog waits at a locked door.
signals.next: Write one hour card, including Sunday, and one line: appointment preferred, call or text ahead. Copy it to Google, Yelp, and the contact page the same morning.

signals.note: The work is in the reviews. Neighbors talk about rescue dogs, huskies, and a peaceful shop. The site photos help. Public listings do not clearly show this week's grooms the way a first-time owner would need.
signals.next: Put four current photos on Google: the suite door, the table, a nervous dog who left calm, and a finished groom.

signals.note: csgalpine.com loads and belongs to you. Services, about, and contact are there. Leftover Wix chrome is still public: top of page, bottom of page, and a 4k+ Happy Customers block on a shop registered in October 2024. There is no book button. Hours are missing. A phone visitor has to hunt for the number.
signals.next: Put the phone, the suite, and the appointment line above the fold. Cut the leftover counters. The brochure can stay. The book-now door is still call or text.

signals.note: Name and phone line up. The contact page says 2065 Arnold Way, STE #102. Yahoo, Nextdoor, and Yellow Pages often drop the suite. MapQuest has #102. Two doors in the same building is how a neighbor walks into the wrong unit.
signals.next: Put Suite 102 on Google, Yelp, and the directories. Street and phone are already doing their job.
